result.title: Text-Only Domain Adaptation for Low-Resource Medical ASR: Shallow Fusion and Density Ratio Rescoring for Hausa
result.summary: Automatic speech recognition (ASR) systems often struggle with specialised medical vocabulary, especially in low-resource languages where domain-specific speech data are scarce. We investigate text-only domain adaptation for Hausa medical ASR using the fixed MMS-1B-FL102 acoustic model and two decoding-time language-model fusion methods: Shallow Fusion (SF) and the Density Ratio Approach (DRA). A 4-gram KenLM trained on 19,421 Hausa health sentences serves as the medical target model, while a 75,372-sentence general-domain model provides the source prior for DRA. Evaluation uses 250 recordings of 25 physician-reviewed prompts from 10 speakers across six northern Nigerian states. Under prompt-disjoint five-fold cross-validation, SF and DRA reduce WER from 29.56% to 23.55% and 23.33%, respectively. Both significantly outperform greedy decoding (p < 0.001), while their difference is not significant (p = 0.423). However, general-LM-only SF achieves 23.96% WER, indicating that the medical LM's additional improvement over a general LM is modest. Medical Term Error Rate also improves under fusion, but does not establish a distinct medical-domain advantage. These findings demonstrate that lightweight, text-only language-model fusion can improve Hausa medical ASR without additional domain-specific speech collection.

AI.brief_summary: 该文研究豪萨语医疗语音识别的纯文本域适应，在冻结的 MMS-1B 声学模型上用 4-gram KenLM 做 Shallow Fusion 与 Density Ratio（DRA）解码期融合，WER 从 29.56% 降至约 23.3%，但与仅用通用语言模型的融合相比增益有限。
AI.relevance_reason: 该方法不涉及视觉或 latent 推理状态，但「密度比」以通用模型为源先验扣除、只保留目标域特有增益，可能为 LVR 中区分通用先验与推理内容实际贡献（贡献分配）提供一种可核查的度量思路。
